tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P1] Build the accumulateTouchChips pure module
tasks.description:
Create `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/lib/touch-chips.ts` — a pure, DOM-free module that folds a message's `MessagePart[]` into a deduplicated `TouchChip[]`. Export the `TouchChip` interface exactly as specified:

```ts
export interface TouchChip {
  key: string; // normalized target identity (abs path or normalized URL or command)
  kind: 'file' | 'url' | 'command';
  label: string; // basename / domain / command
  fullTarget: string; // full path / URL for tooltip + canvas open
  verb: 'read' | 'search' | 'edit' | 'create' | 'delete' | 'fetch' | 'run';
  live: boolean; // any contributing tool_call still pending/running
  error: boolean;
  touches: number; // dedup counter
  additions?: number;
  deletions?: number; // net, edits only
  upgraded?: boolean; // read→edit transition happened (drives morph)
  firstSeq: number;
  lastSeq: number; // ordering for chronological lens
  history: string[]; // tooltip audit trail ("read ×2, then edited +12 −4")
}

export function accumulateTouchChips(parts: MessagePart[]): TouchChip[];
```

`MessagePart` (import from `@dorkos/shared/types`) `tool_call` variant fields available: `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `input?: string` (JSON-encoded), `result?: string`, `status: 'pending' | 'running' | 'complete' | 'error'`. `firstSeq`/`lastSeq` are the part's index position in the `parts` array (there is no separate seq field on the wire type — use array index as the ordering key, since parts already arrive in chronological order).

Algorithm: iterate `parts` in order, for every `tool_call` part with a mappable `toolName`, derive `(key, kind, verb, target)` per this table, then append-then-merge into a `Map<string, TouchChip>` keyed by `key` — never overwrite by "latest tool state", always fold the new touch into the existing chip's counters/history (Cursor's silent-drop bug is the cautionary tale named in the spec).

Tool → verb/target mapping (parse `input` as JSON; on parse failure, skip the part — never throw):
- `Read`, `Glob` → verb `read`; target = `input.file_path` (Read) or `input.pattern` (Glob, the pattern string itself is the chip's target/label, kind `file`).
- `Grep` → verb `search`; target = `input.pattern`; label = the pattern in quotes; kind `command`. If `result` is parseable for a hit count (look for a leading integer or "N matches"/"N lines" pattern in the result text — the Grep tool's result is plain text, so this is best-effort regex, e.g. count lines in `result` as a fallback), surface it via `history`; when not parseable, omit hit-count details.
- `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `NotebookEdit` → verb `edit`; target = `input.file_path`; kind `file`. Diffstat: this feature has no `structuredPatch` field anywhere in `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts` or the tool_call result shape — do NOT reference one. Instead, for `Edit`, parse `input.old_string` / `input.new_string` (present on the JSON-encoded `input`, same fields `OutputRenderer.tsx`'s `parseEditInput` at `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/message/OutputRenderer.tsx:46-63` already parses) and compute a line-count diffstat: `additions` = new lines not in old (via a simple LCS-free heuristic: split both strings on `\n`, `additions = max(0, newLines.length - commonPrefixSuffixOverlap)`, `deletions` analogous) — a coarse but deterministic count is acceptable; precision is not required, only monotonic accumulation across edits. For `MultiEdit`, sum the diffstat across its `input.edits[]` array (each entry has `old_string`/`new_string`). For `NotebookEdit`, if `old_string`/`new_string`-shaped fields are absent, omit `additions`/`deletions` (undefined, not zero) rather than fabricate numbers. Accumulate `additions`/`deletions` net across every edit touching the same key (running sum, not replacement).
- `Write` → target = `input.file_path`; kind `file`. Verb `create` if the result indicates a new file, else `edit`. Detection: Claude Code's Write tool result text distinguishes "File created successfully" (new) from an update message mentioning the file already existed — parse `result` for the substring "created" (case-insensitive) to mean `create`, anything else parseable as success means `edit`. Document this heuristic with an inline comment since it depends on runtime-specific result phrasing (verify against the real message list in a browser once Phase 1 UI exists — flag as a follow-up if the phrasing turns out to differ by runtime).
- `Bash` → verb `run`; target = the raw command string (`input.command`); kind `command`. Additionally, best-effort parse `rm` / `git rm` invocations out of the command string (split on `&&`, `;`, `|` to find sub-commands starting with `rm ` or `git rm `; extract trailing path arguments, handling `-rf`/`-r`/`-f` flags and quoted paths with a simple shell-word tokenizer — do not attempt full shell parsing). Each parsed path becomes an independent `delete`-verb chip (kind `file`, key = the path) merged into the same accumulator pass. Unparseable `rm` invocations produce no delete chip (never guess a path).
- `WebFetch` → verb `fetch`; target = `input.url`; key = the URL with its `#hash` fragment stripped (URL parse, drop `.hash`, keep everything else including query string); label = the registrable domain (host minus a single leading `www.`); kind `url`.
- `WebSearch` → verb `search`; target = `input.query`; label = `🔍 ${query}`; kind `command`.
- `Task`/`Agent`, `TodoWrite`, and any `mcp__*` tool name → excluded entirely (v1 scope, per spec Non-Goals).

Verb precedence on merge (when a key gets touched by more than one verb across its history): `delete` > `create` > `edit` > everything else — a chip's final `verb` is the highest-precedence verb it has seen, never a later lower-precedence touch reverting it (e.g. a file `read` then `edited` shows `edit`, and stays `edit` even if read again afterward). When a chip transitions from `read` to `edit` for the first time, set `upgraded = true` exactly once (never re-trigger on subsequent edits to the same file).

`live`: true if any contributing tool_call for this key currently has `status === 'pending' || status === 'running'`. `error`: true if any contributing tool_call has `status === 'error'`. `touches`: increment once per folded tool_call part that maps to this key (this is the `×N` count). `history`: append one human-readable entry per touch, e.g. `read`, `edited +12 −4`, `read ×2, then edited +12 −4` — build this incrementally as a formatted array of strings, one per touch event, so the tray tooltip can join them.

Output ordering: `accumulateTouchChips` returns chips in **first-touch order** (ascending `firstSeq`) by default — callers needing chronological-by-last-touch or kind-grouped order (the tray's toggle) sort the returned array themselves; the accumulator itself does not need a sort parameter.

Acceptance criteria: the module has zero React/DOM imports (verify with `pnpm --filter @dorkos/client typecheck` after adding — no JSX, no `motion/react`, no `document`/`window` references), exports `TouchChip` and `accumulateTouchChips` as named exports, and every branch above is implemented (no `// TODO` stubs — this repo's Hard Rules forbid lingering TODOs).

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P1] Write exhaustive unit tests for accumulateTouchChips
tasks.description:
Create `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/lib/__tests__/touch-chips.test.ts` (Vitest, no DOM — this is a pure-function test, follow the existing sibling pattern in `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/lib/__tests__/`). Build `MessagePart[]` fixtures directly (tool_call parts with `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `input` as JSON strings, `result`, `status`) — do not import React test utilities.

Required scenarios, each as its own `it()`/`describe()` block, testing `accumulateTouchChips` from `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/lib/touch-chips.ts`:

1. **Dedup by path**: two `Read` tool_call parts with the same `file_path` produce exactly one chip with `touches: 2`.
2. **Dedup by URL normalization**: two `WebFetch` parts with URLs differing only by `#hash` fragment (e.g. `https://example.com/page#section1` vs `https://example.com/page#section2`) produce one chip; `key` has no hash; `label` is the registrable domain.
3. **Read→edit upgrade**: a `Read` part followed by an `Edit` part on the same `file_path` produces one chip with `verb: 'edit'`, `upgraded: true`. A third touch (another `Edit`) on the same file does NOT re-set `upgraded` from false back to true or duplicate the upgrade — assert it stays `true` (already-true, not re-triggered).
4. **Net diffstat accumulation**: two `Edit` parts on the same file each with different `old_string`/`new_string` produce a chip whose `additions`/`deletions` are the sum across both edits, not just the last one.
5. **`rm` parsing — plain**: a `Bash` part with `input.command: 'rm foo.txt'` produces a `delete`-verb chip with `fullTarget` (or key) `foo.txt`, plus the `run` chip for the Bash command itself.
6. **`rm` parsing — flags**: `rm -rf dist/` and `rm -r -f build/` both extract the path correctly, ignoring the flag tokens.
7. **`rm` parsing — multiple args**: `rm a.txt b.txt c.txt` produces three delete chips.
8. **`rm` parsing — quoted paths**: `rm "path with spaces.txt"` extracts the full quoted path as one target, not split on the interior space.
9. **`rm` parsing — git rm**: `git rm tracked-file.ts` also produces a delete chip.
10. **`rm` parsing — non-rm commands produce no delete chip**: `Bash` with `input.command: 'pnpm test'` produces only the `run` chip, no delete chip.
11. **Write — new file**: a `Write` part whose `result` text contains "created" (e.g. `'File created successfully at: /tmp/new.ts'`) produces a chip with `verb: 'create'`.
12. **Write — existing file**: a `Write` part whose `result` does not contain "created" produces a chip with `verb: 'edit'`.
13. **Error tint propagation**: a tool_call part with `status: 'error'` produces a chip with `error: true`; a chip touched by both a successful and a failed tool_call on the same key still has `error: true` (error is sticky, not overwritten by a later success).
14. **Chronological vs kind ordering**: given chips touched in a specific order, assert the returned array's default order is ascending `firstSeq` (first-touch order); separately assert that sorting the result by `kind` then by `firstSeq` (the ordering the tray's kind view will apply) produces the expected grouping — this test documents the contract the tray code in task 1.6 relies on, it does not require the accumulator itself to expose a sort mode.
15. **×N counting**: three `Read` parts on the same file produce `touches: 3` and a `history` array with 3 entries (or one summarizing entry mentioning `×3` — assert against whatever format `1.1` implemented, this test locks that format in).
16. **URL hash stripping**: `https://a.com/x?q=1#frag` and `https://a.com/x?q=1` dedup to the same chip (query string preserved, hash stripped).
17. **Verb precedence**: a file that is `read`, then `edited`, then `read` again keeps `verb: 'edit'` (edit-wins, precedence is `delete > create > edit > everything`).
18. **Excluded tools**: `TodoWrite`, `Task`, and an `mcp__foo__bar` tool_call part produce zero chips.
19. **Malformed input JSON**: a tool_call part with unparseable `input` (e.g. `'{not json'`) is skipped without throwing.

Run `pnpm vitest run apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/lib/__tests__/touch-chips.test.ts` to verify all pass before moving on. This is the highest-value test file in the feature — do not under-cover it; every row of the mapping table in `specs/chat-touch-chips/02-specification.md` needs at least one asserting test.

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P1] Build static TouchChip and TouchChipStrip components
tasks.description:
Create the new FSD slice `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/chips/` with two files (plus a barrel `index.ts` if the slice needs one — check the sibling `ui/tools/` and `ui/primitives/` folders in this same feature for the barrel convention already in use and match it):

**`TouchChip.tsx`** — renders one `TouchChip` (the type from `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/lib/touch-chips.ts`, task 1.1) as a `button` element (plain `<button>` in this phase — the `motion.button` pop-in spring lands in Phase 2, task 2.1). Props: `{ chip: TouchChip; onOpen: (chip: TouchChip) => void }`. Renders: a verb icon (📖 read, 🔍 search, ✏️ edit, ✚ create, 🗑 delete, 🌐 fetch, ▮ run — match the emoji glyphs used in the spec's verb table at `specs/chat-touch-chips/04-design-decisions.md` section 5), the chip's `label`, an `×N` badge when `touches > 1`, and a diffstat badge (`+A −D` in green/red, using the existing `text-*` color tokens — never hardcoded hex, per `.claude/rules/components.md`) when `additions`/`deletions` are defined. Deleted chips (`verb === 'delete'`) render as ghosted + `line-through` (the tombstone state — persists, never removed from the DOM once created, per spec "deletions are never invisible"). Error chips (`chip.error`) get a destructive-tinted border/background using existing design tokens (check `layers/shared/ui/` for the existing error/destructive color classes used elsewhere in this feature, e.g. `ErrorMessageBlock.tsx`, and reuse them — don't invent new ones). A `title` attribute (native tooltip, no new tooltip primitive needed for this phase) shows the joined `chip.history` array — this becomes the richer tooltip experience later if the design calls for it, but native `title` satisfies the spec's "tooltip with history" requirement for now. `data-verb={chip.verb}` and `data-live={chip.live}` attributes on the root element — Phase 3's verb CSS animations key off `data-verb` + a `live` class/attribute, so wire this data attribute now even though no animation reads it yet.

Click handling (canvas integration, required in this phase — not deferred to Phase 2): `onClick={() => onOpen(chip)}`. `TouchChipStrip` (below) implements `onOpen` using `useAppStore().openCanvasDocument` from `@/layers/shared/model` (the hook is re-exported from the app-store barrel; see `apps/client/src/layers/shared/model/app-store/app-store-canvas.ts:96` for the `openCanvasDocument: (content: UiCanvasContent) => void` signature). For `chip.kind === 'file'`, call `openCanvasDocument({ type: 'file', sourcePath: chip.fullTarget })` (the exact discriminated-union shape from `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts:3178-3186` — the field is `sourcePath`, not `path` or `filePath`). For `chip.kind === 'url'`, call `openCanvasDocument({ type: 'url', url: chip.fullTarget })` (shape at `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts:3116-3120`). For `chip.kind === 'command'` (search/run chips with no file/URL target), clicking is a no-op (or shows the command in the native tooltip only — no canvas surface for a bare command string).

Embedded/Obsidian-mode fallback (spec Open Questions, resolved): detect embedded mode the same way the rest of the client does — grep for the existing embedded-mode check used elsewhere (likely `useAppStore` or a dedicated `isEmbedded`/`embeddedMode` flag; search `apps/client/src/layers/shared/model/app-store/` and any `embedded` references in `layers/shared`) and reuse it, don't invent a new detection path. When embedded and canvas is unavailable: URL chips call `window.open(chip.fullTarget, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')` instead of `openCanvasDocument`; file chips become inert (no click handler, `title` tooltip only) — this is the logged assumption from the spec's Open Questions section, revisit when the Obsidian plugin surface is verified per this repo's demo-claim gate (never claim in UI copy that file-chip canvas-open works in the plugin).

**`TouchChipStrip.tsx`** — the orchestrator, mounted in `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/message/AssistantMessageContent.tsx` after the parts render loop (add it as a new element after the `{segments.map(...)}` block in the component's return, gated on `chips.length > 0` so a turn with no tool touches renders nothing extra). Props: `{ parts: MessagePart[] }` (pass `message.parts ?? []`, the same array already destructured at `AssistantMessageContent.tsx:251`). Compute `const chips = useMemo(() => accumulateTouchChips(parts), [parts]);` exactly as the spec specifies (memoized on `parts` identity — `parts` is a new array reference each time the message updates during streaming, so this recomputes only when the message actually changes, not on unrelated re-renders).

This phase implements the **settled** state only (no live row, no pile — those are Phase 2): a single collapsed summary line matching the spec's format `📖 21 · ✏️ 3 +34 −11 · 🌐 9 — show all`, built by grouping `chips` by `kind` and summing counts/diffstats per kind, with a trailing "show all" text button that expands the tray (task 1.5's `ChipTray`, wired here via local `useState<boolean>` for expanded/collapsed — per spec "user expansion state is per-message, not persisted", so plain component state, no store). Do not implement the live row in this task — every chip in Phase 1 renders as if the turn had already completed; live-vs-settled windowing is task 2.1.

Add both files to the FSD slice barrel and update whatever imports `AssistantMessageContent.tsx` currently has for its sibling imports (follow the existing import grouping in that file's header, `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/message/AssistantMessageContent.tsx:1-25`).

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P1] Build the ChipTray component with kind filters and ordering toggle
tasks.description:
Create `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/chips/ChipTray.tsx` in the same slice as task 1.4. Props: `{ chips: TouchChip[]; onOpen: (chip: TouchChip) => void; onClose?: () => void }` (the type `TouchChip` from `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/lib/touch-chips.ts`).

Renders the full deduped roster (every chip in `chips`, via `TouchChip.tsx` from task 1.4, reusing the same `onOpen` click-through wiring), with:

- **Per-kind counter-filters**: a small filter bar above the roster showing `📖 21 / ✏️ 3 / 🌐 9`-style counts (one segment per `kind` present in the current `chips` array — `file` reads/edits/creates, `url` fetches, `command` searches/runs — group and count by `chip.verb` for the filter labels since the spec's example groups by verb glyph, not by the coarser `kind` field; e.g. `📖` groups `verb === 'read'`, `✏️` groups `verb === 'edit'`, etc.). Clicking a filter segment toggles showing only that verb's chips; clicking an active filter again clears it back to "all". Local component state, no store.
- **Order toggle**: `kind ⇄ chronological` — a two-option toggle (reuse an existing toggle/segmented-control primitive from `layers/shared/ui/` rather than building a new one; check for an existing `ToggleGroup` or similar in that barrel before adding anything new). "Kind" order groups chips by `verb` then by `firstSeq` within each group (the default/aggregate view); "chronological" sorts the full flat list by `lastSeq` ascending (the audit-view precedent named in the spec: Claude Code `/diff`'s Current-vs-per-turn lenses). Both are pure client-side `Array.prototype.sort` calls over the `chips` prop — no new derivation module needed, this is presentational logic local to the component.
- **Bounded, self-scrolling**: wrap the roster in a container with `max-h-[240px] overflow-y-auto` (the exact bound the spec calls out at `specs/chat-touch-chips/02-specification.md:108` — "The tray is bounded (max-h-[240px])"). The tray must never grow the transcript's own scroll height; it scrolls internally.
- **ARIA disclosure**: the trigger that opens the tray (in `TouchChipStrip.tsx`, task 1.4's "show all" button) needs `aria-expanded={isOpen}` and should reference the tray via `aria-controls`; the tray container itself gets `role="region"` and an `aria-label` (e.g. "Touched files and links"). This satisfies the spec's explicit ARIA requirement (`02-specification.md:93`: "ARIA disclosure (button[aria-expanded] + role=region)").

No motion/animation in this task — the tray opens/closes instantly via conditional render in this phase (Phase 2 may add an expand transition, but that is out of scope here; do not add `AnimatePresence` yet). Wire `ChipTray` into `TouchChipStrip.tsx` (task 1.4) as the expanded-state render, replacing the settled summary line when `isOpen` is true.

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P1] Component-test the static chip strip, tray, and canvas click-through
tasks.description:
Create `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/chips/__tests__/TouchChipStrip.test.tsx` (and a sibling `ChipTray.test.tsx` if the strip test grows past a reasonable single-file size — follow this repo's 300/500-line file-size guidance in `.claude/rules/conventions.md`). Use React Testing Library + jsdom with a mock `Transport` via `TransportProvider`, matching this repo's established client test pattern (`.claude/rules/testing.md`; see any existing test in `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/__tests__/` for the harness setup, e.g. `MessageItem.test.tsx`).

Required scenarios:

1. **Settled summary line renders**: mount `TouchChipStrip` with `parts` containing a handful of completed `tool_call` parts (Read ×2, Edit ×1, WebFetch ×1) and assert the collapsed summary line text/structure matches the grouped-by-verb format (e.g. contains `📖`, `✏️`, `🌐` glyphs with correct counts) and a "show all" trigger is present.
2. **No chips ⇒ no render**: mount with `parts` containing only a `text` part (no `tool_call`s) and assert `TouchChipStrip` renders nothing (query for its root and expect `null`/empty).
3. **Tray opens on "show all" click**: `userEvent.click` the trigger, assert the tray (roster of individual chips) becomes visible, and the trigger's `aria-expanded` flips to `true`.
4. **Tray filters by verb**: with chips of at least two different verbs, click a filter segment and assert only chips of that verb render; click again and assert all chips return.
5. **Tray order toggle**: assert the DOM order of rendered chips changes between "kind" and "chronological" modes (construct fixture parts where the two orderings produce a detectably different sequence, e.g. an edit that happened first chronologically but sorts after a later read in kind-then-firstSeq order — pick concrete firstSeq/lastSeq values that make the two orders provably different).
6. **ARIA correctness**: assert the tray container has `role="region"` and an accessible name, and the trigger button has `aria-expanded` reflecting open state.
7. **Chip click calls openCanvasDocument with the right UiCanvasContent**: mock/spy `useAppStore` (or the store's `openCanvasDocument`, following whatever mocking convention this repo's existing chat tests use for `useAppStore` — search for `vi.mock` of the app-store module in an existing test like `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/__tests__/` for the pattern) and assert clicking a file chip calls it with `{ type: 'file', sourcePath: <the file path> }` and clicking a URL chip calls it with `{ type: 'url', url: <the url> }`.
8. **Reduced-motion renders no looping animation classes**: with `prefers-reduced-motion` simulated (however this repo's existing tests mock `useReducedMotion` from `motion/react` — check for an existing mock pattern before inventing one; if none exists, mock the hook to return `true` for this test) assert no `data-verb`-driven CSS animation class is applied to a live chip's root element. (Phase 1 has no live state yet, so this assertion may be a lighter placeholder here — e.g. asserting the static chip never carries a looping-animation class regardless — and gets its real teeth in Phase 3's tests once the verb CSS lands; note this explicitly in the test file's description so it isn't mistaken for full Phase 3 coverage.)

Run `pnpm vitest run apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/chips/__tests__/TouchChipStrip.test.tsx` (and the `ChipTray` test file if split out) to confirm all pass. jsdom cannot verify animation feel — that verification is explicitly deferred to the Phase 3 dev-playground/simulator work per the spec's Testing Strategy section, not this task.

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P2] Add live-row windowing and pop-in spring to the chip strip
tasks.description:
Extend `TouchChipStrip.tsx` (`apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/chips/`, built in task 1.4) with the **live** lifecycle state: while the message is streaming and at least one chip has `live: true`, render a bounded row of the newest ≤4 live-or-recently-touched chips (order by `lastSeq` descending, take 4, then re-reverse for left-to-right newest-on-the-right display — matching spec `02-specification.md:90`: "live (row of newest ≤4 live-or-recent chips, pile on the left)"). Chips beyond the 4-window are NOT yet removed from the DOM in this task — task 2.2 (`ChipPile`) handles what happens to them (the absorption exit + pile landing); this task's job is purely the row's windowing logic and the entry animation for new chips arriving into the row.

Convert `TouchChip.tsx`'s root element from a plain `<button>` (task 1.4) to `motion.button` (import `motion` from `motion/react`, already installed — see `AssistantMessageContent.tsx:2` for the existing import pattern in this same feature). Add the pop-in spring exactly as specified: `initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 7 }}`, `animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}`, `transition={{ type: 'spring', stiffness: 320, damping: 28 }}` (verbatim values from `specs/chat-touch-chips/02-specification.md:91` and `04-design-decisions.md:38`, which describes "slight overshoot" — the given stiffness/damping combination produces that overshoot, don't retune it). This animation must run only when a chip newly enters the live row (a new chip arriving, i.e. `key` not present in the previous render's visible set), never on every re-render — use the chip's stable `key` as the React `key` prop on the `motion.button` so mount/unmount (not just prop changes) drives the `initial`/`animate` transition, which is how `motion/react` naturally scopes entry animations to first mount.

Wire `useReducedMotion` from `motion/react` (the spec calls out `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` is already configured somewhere in the app shell — find where via `grep -rn "reducedMotion" apps/client/src` and confirm it wraps the tree the chip strip renders under; if it already wraps the whole app, `useReducedMotion()` inside `TouchChip.tsx` returns the right value automatically). When reduced motion is active, the pop-in becomes a simple opacity fade (`initial={{opacity:0}}`, `animate={{opacity:1}}`, no `y` offset, per spec `04-design-decisions.md:73`: "absorption/entry become simple fades").

Determining live-vs-settled for the whole strip: the strip is in **live** mode when any chip has `live: true`; it transitions to **settled** mode (task 1.4's collapsed summary line) once every chip has `live: false` — this task only needs to implement the live-row rendering path; the actual settle *transition* animation (live row collapsing into the summary line) is task 2.3, not this one. For this task, a hard swap between live-row and settled-line is acceptable as an interim state.

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P2] Build ChipPile with absorption exit and wobble
tasks.description:
Create `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/chips/ChipPile.tsx` in the same slice (task 1.4's location). Renders the facepile: an overlapping stack of up to 3 mini-chip glyphs (small circular/rounded tiles showing just the verb icon or first letter, overlapping via negative margin, `-space-x-*` utility or equivalent — check `layers/shared/lib/` or existing avatar-stack patterns in the codebase, e.g. anything using `resolveAgentVisual` for a precedent on stacked-avatar styling, before inventing new overlap math) plus a count badge showing the total number of chips currently in the pile (not just the visible 3). Props: `{ chips: TouchChip[]; onExpand: () => void }` — clicking anywhere on the pile calls `onExpand` (wired to open the `ChipTray` from task 1.5, same trigger semantics as the settled line's "show all").

**Absorption**: when a chip ages out of `TouchChipStrip`'s live-row window (task 2.1 — the newest-4 cutoff), it does not just disappear; wrap the live row in `AnimatePresence` (from `motion/react`) and give the exiting chip's `motion.button` an `exit` animation: `exit={{ x: -16, scale: 0.45, opacity: 0 }}` over `250ms` (verbatim from spec `02-specification.md:94`: "exit x:-16, scale:.45, opacity:0 over 250ms + pile wobble is the ported mockup behavior" — do not attempt the rejected `layoutId`-anchor-to-pile-position approach the spec explicitly calls "overkill").

**Wobble**: when `ChipPile`'s count increments (a chip finishes absorbing), the pile itself does a brief wobble — a CSS keyframe or a `motion` `animate` sequence on the pile's root (e.g. `rotate: [0, -4, 3, 0]` over ~300ms triggered by a `key` bump on the count, or a CSS `@keyframes wobble` added to `apps/client/src/index.css` under a new `/* touch chips */` comment block per spec `02-specification.md:99` — this block header is shared with Phase 3's verb animations, so if this task lands first, start the block; Phase 3 tasks append to it, they don't create a competing block). Trigger the wobble once per landing event, not continuously (motion means in-progress is the read/search/edit verb loops' job — the pile wobble is a discrete landing acknowledgment, not a loop).

Under reduced motion (`useReducedMotion()`), both the absorption exit and the wobble collapse to simple fades/no-op per the same grammar rule as task 2.1.

Wire `ChipPile` into `TouchChipStrip.tsx`'s live-row rendering (task 2.1): render it to the left of the live row (matching spec's "pile on the left"), fed the set of chips that have aged out of the 4-window.

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P2] Implement the upgrade morph and live-to-settled settle transition
tasks.description:
Two related lifecycle transitions, both in `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/chips/`:

**Upgrade morph** (in `TouchChip.tsx`, task 1.4): when a chip's `upgraded` flag flips from `false`/`undefined` to `true` (the read→edit transition from `accumulateTouchChips`, task 1.1), animate the icon flip + one expanding ring pulse — per spec `04-design-decisions.md:65`: "icon flips read→edit with a single expanding ring pulse; diffstat slides in" and `02-specification.md:100`: "upgrade morph (icon flip + one ring pulse)". Implementation: drive this off a `key` change on the icon element (e.g. `key={chip.upgraded ? 'edit-icon' : 'read-icon'}` inside an `AnimatePresence mode="wait"` or a `motion.span` with an `animate` triggered by watching `chip.upgraded` via `useEffect`) so the morph fires exactly once — the spec is explicit that this is "driven by a key change, not re-render" (`02-specification.md:86`). Add the ring pulse as a `motion.span` absolutely positioned over the icon, `initial={{ scale: 0.6, opacity: 0.8 }}`, `animate={{ scale: 1.8, opacity: 0 }}`, `transition={{ duration: 0.3 }}`, unmounted after the transition completes (use `onAnimationComplete` to remove it from the tree, or key it so `AnimatePresence` handles the unmount — do not leave a permanently-mounted pulse element). The diffstat badge "slides in": animate its `initial={{opacity:0, x:-4}}` → `animate={{opacity:1, x:0}}` alongside the morph.

**Settle transition** (in `TouchChipStrip.tsx`, task 1.4/2.1): when the strip's mode flips from live (task 2.1) to settled (the collapsed summary line, task 1.4) — i.e. the last live chip finishes — animate the live row + pile collapsing into the summary line rather than the hard swap task 2.1 left as an interim state. Wrap both the live-row container and the settled-line container in `AnimatePresence`, giving the live row an `exit={{ opacity: 0, height: 0 }}` and the settled line an `initial={{ opacity: 0 }}` fade-in, `transition={{ duration: 0.3, ease: [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1] }}` (reuse the exact easing curve already used for tool-call auto-hide in `AssistantMessageContent.tsx:96` — `[0.4, 0, 0.2, 1]` — for consistency across the message list's collapse animations rather than inventing a new curve).

Both transitions respect `useReducedMotion()`: the morph becomes an instant icon swap with no ring pulse (opacity cross-fade only), and the settle transition becomes an instant opacity swap with no height animation.
tasks.activeForm: Implementing the upgrade morph and live-to-settled settle transition

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P2] Handle virtualizer re-measure and test the full lifecycle
tasks.description:
**Virtualizer re-measure**: `MessageList.tsx` (`apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/MessageList.tsx`) uses TanStack Virtual with dynamic measurement. `TouchChipStrip`'s height changes across its three states (no chips → live row appears → tray expands to `max-h-[240px]`), and per spec `02-specification.md:108`, these changes must trigger a bounded re-measure, following "the existing pattern used by tool-card expand (measureElement on transition end)". Find that existing pattern: grep `MessageList.tsx` and `AutoHideToolCall`/`ToolCallCard`-adjacent code for how a tool card's expand/collapse triggers the virtualizer's `measureElement` (likely a `ref` callback or a `ResizeObserver` hookup already wired for tool-card auto-hide's height animation at `AssistantMessageContent.tsx:93-98`). Apply the identical mechanism to `TouchChipStrip`'s root — call the virtualizer's re-measure at the same lifecycle points (transition end of the live→settled collapse from task 2.3, and tray open/close from task 1.5) rather than on every animation frame. Confirm no `overflow-anchor` changes are needed (spec explicitly rules this out at `02-specification.md:108`) — do not add any `overflow-anchor` CSS.

**Full-lifecycle component tests**: extend or add to `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/chips/__tests__/` covering the motion-bearing behaviors that task 1.6 deliberately deferred:
1. A chip transitions from `live: true` to `live: false` mid-test (simulate by re-rendering `TouchChipStrip` with updated `parts` where a tool_call's `status` flips from `running` to `complete`) and assert the strip settles (summary line appears, live row unmounts).
2. A 5th chip's arrival ages the 1st out of the live-row window — assert the pile's count increments and the aged-out chip is no longer in the live row's DOM (whether via checking `AnimatePresence` exit completion with fake timers, or asserting the pile-fed chip set, per whatever this repo's existing tests do for `AnimatePresence` exit assertions — search for an existing test asserting on a `motion` exit, e.g. around `AutoHideToolCall`'s tests, for the established pattern of advancing fake timers past an exit transition).
3. A read→edit upgrade fires the morph exactly once even across multiple subsequent edits to the same file (re-render with 3 sequential edits on the same path, assert whatever DOM/class signal indicates "morph fired" only appears/changes once).
4. `MessageList`'s virtualizer re-measure is invoked when a message's `TouchChipStrip` changes height (mock or spy the virtualizer's `measureElement` call, following the existing virtualizer test setup in `MessageList`'s own test file if one exists — check `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/__tests__/` for a `MessageList` test that already exercises `measureElement`).

Run `pnpm vitest run apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/chips/__tests__/` and the relevant `MessageList` test file to confirm everything passes.

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P3] Add the seven verb CSS animations and reduced-motion fallbacks
tasks.description:
Add the verb-specific continuous-loop animations to `apps/client/src/index.css`, in the `/* touch chips */` block (started in task 2.2 if that task landed first — append to it, don't create a duplicate block; if 2.2 didn't add CSS, create the block now). Normative source for exact timing/easing/choreography: `specs/chat-touch-chips/mockups/04-verb-vocabulary.html` and `specs/chat-touch-chips/mockups/05-verbs-search-delete-round2.html` — open both in a browser and **port, not copy**: the mockup CSS uses infinite loops and fixed pixel slots for demo purposes; the real implementation must gate every loop on `data-verb` + a live/in-progress condition so animation runs only while `chip.live === true` and stops the instant the tool settles (spec grammar rule, `04-design-decisions.md:71`: "Motion means in-progress; stillness means done").

Seven animations, each scoped to `.chip-*` classes keyed off the `data-verb` attribute already wired on `TouchChip.tsx`'s root (task 1.4):

1. **Read — the scan**: `[data-verb='read'][data-live='true']` gets a soft highlight band that sweeps smoothly across the chip (a `::before` or `::after` pseudo-element with a gradient, animated `transform: translateX` across the chip's width, looping while live).
2. **Search — the beam**: `[data-verb='search'][data-live='true']` gets one smooth angled (skewed, e.g. `skewX(-20deg)`) light beam sweeping through. **Beam only — no hit-marks or underlines** (the spec is explicit this was rejected in round 2: `04-design-decisions.md:59` and `:67`).
3. **Edit — the scribble**: `[data-verb='edit'][data-live='true']` gets a pencil-icon wiggle (small rotate keyframe) plus a blinking caret in the filename (reuse the existing `@keyframes blink-cursor` at `apps/client/src/index.css:581` if its shape fits, rather than defining a near-duplicate). The diffstat digits ticking up live is NOT a CSS animation — it's a `motion` spring on the number's value change in `TouchChip.tsx` (`animate` a `motion.span` keyed to the additions/deletions value using `motion/react`'s number-interpolation, not "the mockup's fake odometer" per spec `02-specification.md:98-100`). Implement that spring here alongside the CSS if not already present from task 2.3.
4. **Create — border-draw + spark**: `[data-verb='create'][data-live='true']` gets the chip border drawing itself around empty space via SVG `stroke-dashoffset` animation (an inline `<svg>` rect outline inside the chip, `stroke-dasharray`/`stroke-dashoffset` animated from full-offset to zero), the name fading in inside it, and one green spark (a small radial burst, single-shot on mount, not looping — this is the one verb whose "loop" is actually a single construction animation since a create only happens once).
5. **Delete — bin-swallow**: `[data-verb='delete']` gets the filename compressing/skewing as it's "sucked" into the trash icon (`transform: scale + skew` keyframe on the label text), a tiny puff (small fading circle burst), and the bin does a satisfied chomp (a small icon squash-and-stretch). This is single-shot (delete chips don't loop — they animate once into the tombstone state and then sit still, ghosted + struck-through, per task 1.4's static tombstone rendering).
6. **Fetch — the ping**: `[data-verb='fetch'][data-live='true']` gets radar rings emanating from the favicon-tile position (expanding, fading circles, staggered) plus three dots streaming downward beside the domain (a small bouncing-dots keyframe, similar in spirit to the existing `@keyframes typing-dot` at `apps/client/src/index.css:568` — reuse or adapt rather than reinventing).
7. **Run — terminal pulse**: `[data-verb='run'][data-live='true']` gets a monospace chip styling, a blinking block cursor (reuse `@keyframes blink-cursor` at `apps/client/src/index.css:581` directly), and a faint green heartbeat pulse on the border (reuse or adapt the existing `@keyframes health-pulse` at `apps/client/src/index.css:919` if its rhythm fits a "heartbeat" description).

**Grammar rules to enforce across all seven** (per `04-design-decisions.md:69-74`): every live animation stays inside the chip's own bounds (no `transform` that overflows into layout, no neighbor-shifting side effects); durations for entries/transitions follow the 100-300ms band already documented in `.claude/rules/components.md`, only the continuous in-progress loops (scan, beam, ping) run longer cycles (the mockups show roughly 1.5-2.5s loop periods — match what's in the mockup files, don't guess).

**Reduced-motion fallback**: add a single `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block (or use the existing `useReducedMotion()` React-side gating already wired in tasks 2.1-2.3 for the `motion`-driven pieces, plus a CSS media query for the pure-CSS loops) that replaces every one of the seven loops with a static icon + a single subtle opacity pulse (reuse `@keyframes breathe` or the new `animate-tasks` from task 1.3 rather than adding an eighth new keyframe for this fallback state).

5. **ChipPile**: the pile component (task 2.2) with a representative count and the facepile stack, plus a button to trigger the wobble on demand (call whatever prop/handler makes the pile re-wobble, so a visual reviewer can watch it fire repeatedly without reloading).
6. **ChipTray**: the tray (task 1.5) pre-populated with a realistic mixed roster (10-20 chips across all kinds) showing the filter bar and kind⇄chronological toggle in action.

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P3] Add the touch-chips simulator scenario with bursty arrivals
tasks.description:
Create `apps/client/src/dev/simulator/scenarios/touch-chips.ts`, following the exact structure of the existing `apps/client/src/dev/simulator/scenarios/multi-tool-chain.ts` (read it in full first — it's the closest precedent: a `SimScenario` object with an `id`, `title`, `description`, and a `steps` array built from `createUserMessage`/`createAssistantMessage`/`createToolCall` helpers from `apps/client/src/dev/mock-chat-data.ts`, plus step types like `append_message`, `set_status`, `append_tool_call`, `update_tool_call` with `delayMs` timing).

Required scenario shape, per spec `02-specification.md:119`: "bursty arrivals (3 tools in 1s, idle 10s, more), read-then-edit same file, an `rm`, a WebFetch batch — exercising absorption timing end-to-end":

1. **Bursty arrival burst 1**: 3 tool calls (e.g. Read, Grep, Read on different files) appended with `delayMs` values totaling roughly 1000ms between the first `append_tool_call` and the third settling — tight enough that the live row's pile-absorption (task 2.2) has real work to do once a 4th/5th chip arrives.
2. **Idle gap**: a step (or accumulated `delayMs`) simulating roughly 10 seconds of no new tool activity, letting the strip settle visually and demonstrating that live loops (task 3.1) genuinely stop when nothing is pending.
3. **More arrivals**: additional tool calls resuming after the idle gap, pushing the earlier burst's chips further into the pile.
4. **Read-then-edit on the same file**: a `Read` tool call on a specific `file_path`, followed later by an `Edit` tool call on that exact same `file_path` — this is what exercises the upgrade morph (task 2.3) end-to-end in a way unit tests (task 1.2, jsdom-bound) cannot verify.
5. **An `rm`**: a `Bash` tool call with a command like `rm path/to/old-file.ts`, exercising the delete-chip parsing (task 1.1) and the bin-swallow animation (task 3.1) visually.
6. **A WebFetch batch**: 2-3 `WebFetch` tool calls with different URLs (some sharing a domain to exercise dedup/grouping, per task 1.1's URL normalization) fired close together, exercising the fetch/ping verb (task 3.1).

Register the new scenario in `apps/client/src/dev/simulator/scenarios/index.ts` (add `export { touchChips } from './touch-chips';` alongside the existing exports at lines 6-14) and wherever the simulator's scenario picker consumes that barrel (find the consumer — likely `apps/client/src/dev/simulator/` has a scenario-selection UI or registry that imports from `scenarios/index.ts`; grep for an existing scenario name like `multiToolChain` used outside the `scenarios/` folder to find it and add the new one alongside).

This task only needs the accumulator (task 1.1) and the existing simulator step-type infrastructure to write — it does not require the chip UI components to exist first, so it can be built in parallel with task 3.1's CSS work. It becomes fully meaningful for visual verification once 3.1 and the earlier chip components are in place.

tasks.subject: [chat-touch-chips] [P3] Final polish pass against mockups and changelog fragment
tasks.description:
**Polish pass**: with the dev playground showcases (task 3.2) and simulator scenario (task 3.3) both available, do a side-by-side comparison against every mockup in `specs/chat-touch-chips/mockups/` (`01-direction.html` through `05-verbs-search-delete-round2.html`) and the `04-design-decisions.md` design authority doc. Specifically verify: (a) every verb's live animation duration/easing reads as calm, not jittery, per the Calm Tech design language (`contributing/design-system.md`); (b) the pop-in spring's overshoot (task 2.1) matches the mockup's feel, not over- or under-shooting; (c) the pile wobble (task 2.2) reads as a satisfying "landing" acknowledgment, not a jarring shake; (d) the settled summary line's grouped format exactly matches `📖 21 · ✏️ 3 +34 −11 · 🌐 9 — show all` spacing/separator conventions from `04-design-decisions.md:47`; (e) the tray's bounded scroll (task 1.5) never visually steals transcript scroll focus; (f) reduced-motion fallbacks (tasks 2.1-2.3, 3.1) genuinely eliminate all looping motion when toggled, verified in-browser (jsdom cannot check this) — use `pnpm dev:dogfood`, open `/dev/chat`, and toggle the OS/browser reduced-motion setting or this app's own reduced-motion dev toggle if one exists in the simulator (`04-design-decisions.md` mentions "the simulator already has animation toggles to extend" at line 91 — check for and reuse an existing toggle rather than adding a new one). Fix any drift found; this task is allowed to touch any file from tasks 1.1-3.3 to close gaps, but should not introduce new components or new spec scope.

**Changelog fragment**: create a new fragment in `changelog/unreleased/` named `<timestamp-id>-chat-touch-chips.md` (generate the id via `.claude/scripts/id.ts` per this repo's `YYMMDD-HHMMSS` convention — do not hand-write a fake id), following the exact format documented in `changelog/README.md` and the existing example fragments in that folder (e.g. `changelog/unreleased/260715-150825-friendly-auth-error.md` — a YAML frontmatter block with a `covers:` array listing the conventional-commit-style PR title(s) this change covers, followed by a `### Added` or `### Changed` markdown section). Write the user-facing copy per the `writing-for-humans` skill (plain language, no jargon, describes what the user sees, not the implementation) — the spec's suggested line is a strong starting point: "See every file and link your agent touches, live." Expand it slightly to cover the full feature surface (the settling summary + expandable tray + verb-specific motion) in 1-3 sentences, matching the tone and length of neighboring fragments in the same folder.

This is the last task in the feature — after it lands, `specs/chat-touch-chips/` moves toward VERIFY per this repo's `/flow` stage spine.
